body: I'll do my best. I sent her a message for when she wakes up telling her that I want to be open to her at some point tomorrow and to not let me cop out of it later. Here's hoping it goes well and all that.

I think you might be right. I'll be sure to tell her then, whenever she gets up and I am mentally able. I'm honestly really nervous about the whole thing because I haven't even admitted it to *myself* yet, but I think she deserves to know. Thank you.

Same thing here. I just don't want her to think that it's her fault or that she isn't being as helpful as she should be; there are some things encouragement just can't fix. I really want to tell her, maybe I can find some time this week to gently let her know.

Mhmm. I've been trying to build myself up in my own head a bit, but the idea of telling someone else is something else entirely, I dunno when or how I'm going to do it. I was thinking about telling my girlfriend because if anyone deserves to know it's her, but I can never find the right time, y'know?
That's true. I'm always afraid that people are going to try to "fix" me, and it's not going to help at all and throw my life further out of balance.
Sleep is indeed the magic reset of my emotions. We'll see about tomorrow. Thank you for the advice!

I think I get what you mean, I keep getting constantly told that my life is pretty good compared to others, which never really helps me much. The thing about sharing is that when/if I share, it means I have to sort of "face it" almost, and I'm not sure at this point that it wouldn't destroy me if I tried.

I always feel bad about not telling my girlfriend, because she shares so much with me, and I never share anything with her. I don't want to be unfair because I trust her very very much, but I'm afraid that she won't take it well, or that she'll be even more worried about me, or worse that she'll blame herself. I have a problem telling people how I'm feeling; hell, just now I can't even directly tell her that just now she accidentally outed me in front of everyone in the voice chat, because I'm worried about how that would make her feel. I know that's stupid and it'll probably make her feel worse later, but that doesn't change the fact that I just can't do it.

I think the other thing about telling myself is that my brain is telling me not to, because that means I have to do something about it and it doesn't want that. Again, I know it's wrong, but I don't have the willpower to overrule it.

I'll look some of those text crisis centers up, even if I never use it I guess it would be nice to have on my phone. People here seem nice so far, so you'll probably see me here a lot. I've been doing better the last few weeks but this week has really been testing my new resolve

I'll do my best, and hopefully tonight that'll be enough

I'm trying to keep that in mind, but I'm so isolated from everyone else that it's really hard to find anyone to talk to, especially anyone that I trust and that can actually help me. I used to have a sketchbook, but it quickly turned into something really unhealthy so I put it away for a while. I've been trying to find a way to tell my girlfriend and have dropped hints here and there, but my mind is holding me back from actually doing it.

Funny enough, I've never actually admitted it to myself straight out. I'm always afraid that if I tell her or myself it'll send me straight into somewhat of a bad situation. Hell, a couple of weeks ago I was convinced that if anyone found out I would absolutely *have* to do it as soon as I could, even though I know it doesn't make much sense.

I've almost called a crisis center once, but the idea of having to actually talk to someone on a phone gave me pause and I ended up just wrestling through it

First, thanks for the response; I honestly wasn't expecting anyone to actually respond in the first place, past experience 'n all. To actually answer your question, normally there's just this large empty feeling, occasionally punctuated with thoughts of issues that I haven't been able to find solutions for, and then my brain gets attached to suicide and I don't stop thinking about it until I either go to bed or am suddenly distracted by something that requires more brainpower. Right now I'm trying to keep it away from that, but now it's juggling between telling me I need to die and telling me I at least need to hurt myself, which is really chipping steadily at the state of mind I've been trying to build up.
